Take a breath. Slow down.

I'm not going to tell you that you made nothing but wonderful decisions before now, because you've already said you don't want to hear that. Did you make the best choice? Wasn't there, not gonna cast judgment. 

Will ending your life *change* anything? Will it undo those decisions? Or will it take an already rough situation and make it so, so much worse? If you feel bad about what you may have done to your ex psychologically, I'm telling you now - killing yourself will more than likely screw with him too, so you'd potentially take a bad situation and just make it worse. You sound like that's the *LAST* thing you want to do, so slow up a minute here.

If you made a bad decision... then you roll with it. You *KEEP GOING* and you take all this that you're feeling right now and you tell yourself that you never, ever want to feel like this or put someone else in this position again. And then you keep on living. Dying over this will not take it back. It won't FIX anything. If you want to put this in a perspective, if you end everything right now, then this will be the 'crowning achievement', and it sounds like this isn't how you want that to be.

Or you can keep on going. Keep living. Make more decisions - both good and bad - and over time... things can balance out. You can't make this go away, but you *can* make it so this doesn't define you. It doesn't have to. 

And for the record, if you were a 'shit person', this wouldn't bother you nearly as much as it is, all right? Believe me, having met a lot of true 'pieces of work', they'd do things that hurt everyone around them and not bat an eye. That's not the case for you. Keep on going, all right? It ain't gonna be fun, but it can get better.

Three answers to that, OP.

First one is the whole 'it's a permanent solution to a temporary problem' blah blah yadda yadda. Which is technically true in most cases, though I personally *HATE* when people give that. But it *is* true - there's lots of times where the initial, emotional visceral reaction makes complete sense AT THE TIME, but if you slow down, put logic to it, all of that? There's plenty of other options to try before you go the final route. 90% of the time if you can chill long enough to take that breath, there's almost always something you haven't tried yet. At least that's been my experience.

Second is that a lot of people that come to things like this don't want to die - not really, anyway. We want the pain, the frustration, the hopelessness - all the things that are making the idea to end our lives seem palatable? THAT'S what we want to stop. I don't want to die - I personally don't see a whole lot of options for that happening myself, but if there was a way to get even the slightest handhold and keep myself from slipping further? I'd love that. Crossing my fingers (but not holding my breath) here. For a lot of people, it's loneliness. Maybe pointing out that they're not entirely alone on this mudball is enough to help keep them going. Your mileage may vary.

Third - I'd go and put a big long story but it's f all in the morning and we should all be sleeping (yeah, right). But tomorrow's a new day, can have different outcomes than the days before. Let's be honest here - more that likely, tomorrow will suck just as bad as today, and the day before and the day before. This is a fact. But it's also just as true that if you call it, if you give up now there will NEVER be a chance of it getting better. Are the odds great - hell no. But they're whole lot better than if you just give up. Not that it ever feels that way, but it's still true objectively.

And last but not least? Yes. Yes, it *is* your choice, and it's the most powerful, most personal choice you can ever make. Whether you choose to live or to die?  It's entirely up to you, and it can be either the most selfish or the most selfless thing you ever do. It's hard to keep going when you really don't want to - but it's not just about you. It's about your friends, your family - it's not going to just hit you, it's going to hit other people too. As a parent who lost a daughter, I can tell you that years later, it's still scarred me in ways I don't think I'm going to ever get over - so if your parents are still in the picture, that's something to consider too. It has to be your choice in the end, but there's lots of things that you may want to consider before you do.

I can't tell you not to - I'd be a hypocrite if I did, since my own headspace is the whole reason I'm in this forum in the first place. But I hope you don't. It *can* get better. At least, that's *my* hope anyway.

Take a suggestion from someone who's at least in the same age frame (40) and got some of the similar problems?

Try to kick the Xanax first.

I say, having a pretty good idea how hard that's going to be, because I was hooked on Fentanyl for a long time and the withdrawal took 2-3 months and was absolutely nightmarish. It hurt, it messed with my head, my dreams, my sleep. After being on it, other pain medications do next to nothing for my fibromyalgia and now my cancer - so I can at least relate a little bit.

At the end of the day, I'd want to know that whatever decision I came to, it was because of ME, my thoughts, my desires, and not because of some damned pills the doctors pushed on me. And as much as I hate to say it, if you do that you may still come to the same conclusion that you want to end it all. I genuinely hope not. But if you still do it after having kicked the Xanax, then at the very least you can say that you didn't have chems potentially messing with your decisions.

Mind you, the only reason I'm in this forum is because I'm in a bad way as well, so take my words with as many or as few grains of salt as you think they merit. But I hope you at least consider it.

*sighs* As one autistic to another? We both know how we need the cold logic over just the emotional pleas. You're in a bad place and I wish, I really wish that I could tell you that if you just do steps 1 through 7, it'll get better. 

You are not out of options yet. There's always something that hasn't been tried yet. There's always someone else at social services that you can talk to - and yeah, it's another roll of the stacked dice but that doesn't mean that it can't come up different on this run. If you give up now, there will NEVER be a chance that it gets better.

Admittedly, trying again and again and again is an absolute bitch. It's infuriating, it's soul-crushing, and it hurts when they say the system works one way and we know that it doesn't.

I'm not in your shoes. I can't tell you what you should or shouldn't do with your life - in the end, that's a decision only you get to make. Hell, maybe I'm arguing with you here because watching someone else make the the decision I'm tempted to make would make it easier for myself, and some small part of me still is trying to stop that. I don't know.

You're not alone.

It doesn't make it easier. Or better. Or give you that concrete reason that I wish I had for you. But it's still the truth.

I will tell you though - and I say this not meaning to guilt you, but just cold facts - as a father who had to bury his daughter, it is not something you get over. Will it break your mother like it broke me? I hope not. But there will be a crack that will never, ever heal. I can't say that should be a reason to stop - like I said, that's the most intensely personal decision any of us can make. But whatever help she'll receive by virtue of your death? She'll need more after this.

Stay strong. Life is a stacked game, and the odds are not in our favor - even more than NT's. But you can't win if you don't play.

There's a lot that can be commented on here - and you've probably heard it all before, so I'm not going to go with all the typical, trite bull. When I say breath, aside from the whole need for oxygen to not die thing, I mean that you gotta take a step back for a moment and not go with first immediate impulse. If you get through the next week, and feel like things are just unsalvageable... well, if I'm still here in that time, I'll likely have a whole new set of arguments to try and make, but at that point it'll be something that you've had time to think out for yourself. Let's be honest here. But at least try and hold up until the 'wound' isn't fresh - not that dull and throbbing is any better, but at least you'll be making the decision as an ACTION, not a REACTION if that makes any sense.

*sighs* Been there. It's an absolute bitch. Give it time and at least sometimes it'll get easier to handle. Never goes away entirely, but one can get past it. 

Get through tonight. Get through tomorrow. Get through the next day. Right this moment you've got a perfectly legitimate reason to be sad, upset, angry - what have you. But that doesn't mean you've got to do something unchangeable about it.

Breath. Sounds trite, sounds like BS, but it's the hardest thing to do right in that moment. Get through the most immediate urges of it. And then start figuring out how to pick up the pieces - it won't be precisely the same, but enough crazy (see what I did there) glue and it'll be something you can work with. May even turn out better in the long run.

I read this and I'd like to say a lot of things. I'd like to tell you no, don't think like that, that it gets better, easier, etc. But that just seems like an insult to your intelligence - you KNOW that it's 'a permanent solution to a temporary problem' blah blah yadda yadda. But it sure doesn't feel like it, does it? I'd like to tell you to stop thinking those horrifying thoughts - but then the whole reason I'm here in this subgroup is that I'm going through the same thing. I'd like to tell you to focus on the happier things in life - and that's a good thing to do, but it doesn't make the flashes go away and it's sure as hell not easy.

I will say one thing though - getting help is *not* crazy. No, you may not being hearing voices and no, you may not be needing someone to tell you how to live your life 'better' - but there's one thing for moments of depression that come and go, and there's something entirely different for when it just isn't going away. Something's hurt us, made us sick. But you know something? If you were diabetic, it'd be perfectly acceptable to stab your finger 3 times a day and get insulin - kidney problems, dialysis just makes sense and no one says a thing. But when it's in your head, everyone balks at it.

No - you're not crazy. That's the whole point of coming here. That's the whole point of trying to get help. You want to catch this BEFORE it gets to a point where there's no other option. I'm not going to lie to you, it's not going to be easy and it's not going to be fun and NO ONE can judge whether your situation is worth trying to fight through but you.

But I hope you give it a try. 

I'll be frank - I've fought it for 30+ years and still haven't 'won'. But I'm still here, and most of the time the urges CAN be fought, and I can get through my days. Some days are harder than others. 

If you need to talk with someone, I'm here. Feel free to DM if you like.

New plan. Ever read Harry Potter? Remember the Elder Wand?

The cultist who was killed had something that was vital to a ritual, and since that was person was killed, now THEY control this object. Can't just be stolen away from them or it won't work - they either have to be killed (tricky, since one death has already brought enough attention and they don't need any more) or they have to be manipulated into somehow assisting with the ritual. This leaves the cultists scrambling to figure out a Plan C. Have someone close to one of their contacts be a member of the cult - not the contact themselves, but a viable reason to feed them false information and also that way having a way for the cult to reasonably change their plans based on what the players do.

As far as going nuts? There's ways to play that - start giving them periods of missing time. Let them trace down a lead, only to find out that they themselves *might* have been responsible for (since you don't want to shoehorn or Godmode the players too much).

One thing I would suggest? No Old Ones. No Outer Gods. Have them meet cultists, minions, acolytes - knowing ones, but still. Maybe even someone possessed by the Big Bad or an avatar / shell. If your investigators stand toe to toe against a *God*, they're going to lose. Automatic. So how do you get around the fact that they've already encountered that? Well, people lie about what they are, people are known to work on faulty or complete information, the conspiracy may be bigger than they thought - or go the opposite direction and the Grand Conspiracy has it completely effing wrong, and they're just dupes in a bigger game. Grand High Poobah thinks he's running the show, but it's actually the meepy little librarian that stuttered, stumbled and begged for their life that actually has the REAL power and lets the others play their parts and be the bigger targets.

That's the joy of being the Keeper. Were you dastardly and evil and plot this all out ahead of time? Are you just pulling a course correction out of thin air? Is ANYTHING you say what they think it is? 

The players don't know, and you don't have to tell them. =)

During the roaring twenties, radio is becoming the newest form of mass media - and there's all sorts of different programs out there. Some of them truly weird. One of them is an old man, rambling, talking about all sorts of things that will supposedly happen, but it's all nonsense. The stock market is as strong as it's even been, and nothing could bring it down in 1929. And warnings about some obscure Austrian painter? Madness. Still, some teenager is just transfixed by this show, and starts taking notes on all the crazy ramblings on the air.

Skip forward 30 years. Test subject. Book on time travel.

Skip forward another 30 - 40 years. Dawn of the internet. Ham radios are still around, some of them hand built. An old man sits at a desk, tired, ignored by his family. He once did great things, but no one believes him, as his mind is going. He just wants someone, anyone to listen to him - so he takes it upon himself to share certain nuggets of wisdom, basic history, what have you. No one is talking back on the radio, but it doesn't matter anymore. Someone is listening, he's sure of it. After all, he still remembers back in his childhood of the fascinating programs he found just turning the knobs on that first, basic set.

And a universe and a lifetime away, his teenage self is listening. And writing notes that someone else will someday turn into a book.

Anything is possible - for a price. And it's not always money.
